text:
Zach Benson is 21, 5-foot-10, and playing 20:20 a night on Buffalo's top line with Tage Thompson and Jiri Kulich, a trio the Buffalo papers credit with reviving Kulich. That is up from 15:53 last season, with 72% of the Sabres' power-play time now his after 35%. Our numbers flag him as a breakout.

He has 23 points in 25 games and a five-game point streak, but the story is mixed in an interesting way. His goals are behind: five on 10.4 expected, so we call him due. His assists are ahead: Buffalo has scored about 12 more goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, and that is padding his 18 helpers.

What isn't luck is the play driving. The Sabres take 57% of the 5v5 shot attempts and expected goals with him on the ice, 11 points better than without him. Evolving-Hockey had him 98th percentile among forwards for adjusted chance creation last season, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him leaving the zone with possession on 64% of his exits. Those are the habits of a top-line forward, and he has them at 21.
headline: Zach Benson is driving play; the goals lag
